tasks.title: D20 Phase 1 + lockstep: derive the ToolbarScroll wrapper height and update the D19 height assertions
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py, add the named constant TOOLBAR_CONTENT_HEIGHT = 36 (single source of truth) and change the D19 ToolbarScroll QScrollArea's fixed height from the literal 36 to the derived TOOLBAR_CONTENT_HEIGHT + toolbar_scroll.horizontalScrollBar().sizeHint().height() (offscreen 54px; macOS ~52px), keeping toolbar.setFixedHeight(36) and the wrapper's NoFrame / setWidgetResizable(False) / horizontal ScrollBarAsNeeded / vertical ScrollBarAlwaysOff / objectNames / control-and-signal wiring unchanged. Update the D19 height assertions in tests/test_toolbar_scroll_d19.py in lockstep — T53-T04 to the derived relation and min/max == height(), T53-T02's <= 40 bound to the content row — so the suite is never left contradicting D20 (R36).
acceptance_criteria: Structural/mechanism (derived container height — AC-D20.2 mechanism): Given the D20 fix, Then ui/main_window.py defines TOOLBAR_CONTENT_HEIGHT = 36 once, toolbar.setFixedHeight(36) is unchanged (the content row does not grow), and the ToolbarScroll QScrollArea's fixed height equals TOOLBAR_CONTENT_HEIGHT + toolbar_scroll.horizontalScrollBar().sizeHint().height() (a derived value, not the literal 52; offscreen 54px, macOS ~52px); the wrapper keeps NoFrame, setWidgetResizable(False), horizontal ScrollBarAsNeeded, vertical ScrollBarAlwaysOff, objectName 'ToolbarScroll', and the 'MainToolbar' toolbar as its widget; and centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= 750px (the D19 horizontal benefit is unchanged).

tasks.title: D20 Phase 2: add the label-legibility / reserved-lane / as-needed assertions (tests/test_toolbar_d20.py)
tasks.description: Add a new disjoint tests/test_toolbar_d20.py that boots the real offscreen MainWindow (IBApiClient.connect monkeypatched, matching the D19/D20 harness) and asserts the D20 outcome: labels unclipped in both scrollbar states, the derived container height with a 36px content row and a reserved lane below the content, the horizontal scrollbar as-needed in that lane, D19 reachability preserved, and the single-row/inside-central structure. The lane/overlap checks must use the mapped form horizontalScrollBar().mapTo(wrapper, QPoint(0, 0)).y() >= toolbar.height() together with viewport().height() >= toolbar.height() when the scrollbar is shown; geometry() must NOT be used (offscreen it reports top == 0).
acceptance_criteria: AC-D20.1 (labels fully readable; no descender clipped by the scrollbar): Given a shown offscreen window with the toolbar visible, When the toolbar renders (horizontal scrollbar shown at a narrow width and hidden at a wide width), Then for every toolbar QLabel/button text the text's bounding rect lies fully within the toolbar's visible content area and does not intersect the horizontal scrollbar's lane — asserted in both the overflow (shown) and non-overflow (hidden) states — and the content remains a single row.

AC-D20.2 (height supersession — derived container, content row 36px): Given the D20 fix, Then the ToolbarScroll container height equals the derived relation toolbar.height() + wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().sizeHint().height() (offscreen 54px; macOS ~52px) and is < 60px (R35); the toolbar content widget height is TOOLBAR_CONTENT_HEIGHT (36) and has not grown; the reserved lane equals the scrollbar's extent and sits entirely below the content. No hard [50, 52] bound is asserted (the requirement's ~50–52px is the macOS figure; the offscreen derived value is 54px — plan RC-D20-1).

AC-D20.3 (scrollbar as-needed in its reserved lane; B8): Given the D20 fix, When the toolbar content fits (wide window), Then wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().isVisible() is False and the strip height is unchanged (still the derived height); When the content overflows (narrow window), Then it is True and its mapped lane sits below the content row (mapTo(wrapper, QPoint(0,0)).y() >= toolbar.height()).

AC-D20.4 (D19 behaviour preserved): Given the D20 fix, Then the D19 scroll/elide reachability holds: at a narrow window wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().maximum() > 0 and every toolbar control remains a descendant of the scroll content; at a wide window every control lies within the viewport.

AC-D20.5 (single row, no wrap; stays inside the central widget): Given any window width, Then the toolbar content stays a single row (not wrapped) and remains inside the central widget (no QMainWindow.addToolBar / QToolBar); only the horizontal scrollbar occupies the lane below the content.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D20.1 (labels fully readable; no descender clipped by the scrollbar): Given a shown offscreen window with the toolbar visible, When the toolbar renders (horizontal scrollbar shown at a narrow width and hidden at a wide width), Then for every toolbar QLabel/button text the text's bounding rect lies fully within the toolbar's visible content area and does not intersect the horizontal scrollbar's lane — asserted in both the overflow (shown) and non-overflow (hidden) states — and the content remains a single row.
tests.description: At a narrow window (scrollbar shown), for every toolbar label/button text assert the text's mapped bounding rect lies fully within the visible content area and does not intersect the horizontal scrollbar's lane; assert wrapper.viewport().height() >= toolbar.height() and wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().mapTo(wrapper, QPoint(0, 0)).y() >= toolbar.height(). Do not use geometry().
tests.expected_result: No label glyph intersects the scrollbar; the viewport is at least the content-row height and the scrollbar's mapped lane sits below the content.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D20.1 (labels fully readable; no descender clipped by the scrollbar): Given a shown offscreen window with the toolbar visible, When the toolbar renders (horizontal scrollbar shown at a narrow width and hidden at a wide width), Then for every toolbar QLabel/button text the text's bounding rect lies fully within the toolbar's visible content area and does not intersect the horizontal scrollbar's lane — asserted in both the overflow (shown) and non-overflow (hidden) states — and the content remains a single row.

tests.expected_result: Labels are unclipped in the non-overflow (scrollbar-hidden) state too, with the viewport at least the content-row height.

No hard [50, 52] bound is asserted (the requirement's ~50–52px is the macOS figure; the offscreen derived value is 54px — plan RC-D20-1).

Explicitly do NOT assert a literal [50, 52] bound.
tests.expected_result: Container height is the derived value (offscreen 54px, macOS ~52px) and < 60px; content widget stays 36px; the reserved lane is below the content.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D20.3 (scrollbar as-needed in its reserved lane; B8): Given the D20 fix, When the toolbar content fits (wide window), Then wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().isVisible() is False and the strip height is unchanged (still the derived height); When the content overflows (narrow window), Then it is True and its mapped lane sits below the content row (mapTo(wrapper, QPoint(0,0)).y() >= toolbar.height()).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D20.4 (D19 behaviour preserved): Given the D20 fix, Then the D19 scroll/elide reachability holds: at a narrow window wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().maximum() > 0 and every toolbar control remains a descendant of the scroll content; at a wide window every control lies within the viewport.
tests.description: Narrow window: assert wrapper.horizontalScrollBar().maximum() > 0 and every control in the toolbar control list is a descendant of the scroll content. Wide window: assert every control maps within the viewport.
tests.expected_result: Horizontal scroll range > 0 at the narrow width; all controls reachable; every control directly visible at the wide width.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D20.5 (single row, no wrap; stays inside the central widget): Given any window width, Then the toolbar content stays a single row (not wrapped) and remains inside the central widget (no QMainWindow.addToolBar / QToolBar); only the horizontal scrollbar occupies the lane below the content.
tests.description: Assert the toolbar content is a single row (toolbar.height() <= 40, not wrapped); the toolbar is a descendant of centralWidget(); centralWidget().layout().itemAt(0).widget() is the 'ToolbarScroll' QScrollArea; and win.findChildren(QToolBar) == [] (no QMainWindow toolbar area).
tests.expected_result: Content stays one row inside the central widget; only the scrollbar occupies the lane; no addToolBar was used.

tasks.title: D20 Phase 3: full-suite regression gate + real-app manual check
tasks.description: Re-run the full offscreen suite (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen) after the D20 change and confirm zero failures with no D1–D19 regression; re-confirm the D17/D18 criteria in a toolbar-visible window (only vertical space changed — A40) and that centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= 750px and the chart minimum (400px) are preserved; confirm no test connects to live TWS or transmits an order (Q9); and record a manual `python main.py` check that the toolbar labels read clearly with the scrollbar hidden (wide) and shown (narrow) and the strip height is stable in both states (offscreen 54px; macOS ~52px). Per project memory, confirm any intermittent failure with a clean full-suite run before treating it as a regression.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D20.6 (regression, A40): Given the D20 fix, When the full offscreen suite runs (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen), Then it completes with zero failures, every pre-existing D1–D19 acceptance-criteria test still passes, the D17/D18 criteria hold in a toolbar-visible window, and centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= 750px and chart_area >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH (400px) are preserved (only vertical space changed).

R35 (chart vertical space): Given the D20 fix, Then the strip height is < 60px and the chart loses only the reserved lane (~16px macOS / ~18px offscreen) of vertical space — the content row does not grow and the strip does not reach ~60px.
Q9 / no live TWS: Given the D20 batch, Then no automated test connects to live TWS or transmits an order.

tests.expected_result: Zero failures; no D1–D19 regression; D17/D18 criteria hold with the toolbar visible; chart minimum and central min-width preserved.
